title: Rotated Out
description: Refreshing a session is supposed to retire the old boarding pass the moment a new one is issued, not just hand out a spare.
successCondition: Log in, then call POST /api/auth/refresh with the resulting th_refresh cookie. The response sets a new th_refresh cookie. Querying refresh_tokens via `npm run db:psql` shows: the original row now has a non-null revoked_at, and a second row exists for the same user with a null revoked_at whose token_hash differs from the first — the rotation created a new row rather than mutating the old one's hash in place.
hints: apps/api/src/modules/auth/service.ts's refresh() updates the presented token's row to set revokedAt, then calls issueSession() which inserts a fresh row — two DB writes, not one.
You'll need the raw cookie value from the login response to call /refresh — most HTTP clients show Set-Cookie headers in their response inspector.
